summary: Default Flask request instrumentation retained effectively unbounded HTTP path labels; thousands of unmatched paths expanded the relay's application metrics and scrape-serialization cost until Kubernetes OOM-killed the sole 256Mi production relay.
impact: Production was intermittently unavailable during an approximately 87-minute crash loop, with Traefik reporting no available server while the sole relay pod was unavailable; repeated termination also created an unquantified risk of losing active memory-backed relay state, but customer data or work loss was not proven.
fix: Operators mitigated the incident by pausing discovery of only the token.place ServiceMonitor target and replacing the affected pod to obtain a fresh emptyDir, without changing or rolling back the Deployment; the permanent bounded-cardinality fix and deliberate restoration of application scraping remain pending.
lessons: Application metric labels must be bounded and cardinality budgets detected before memory exhaustion; multiprocess files must be safely cleared on container startup, and a single memory-backed relay replica amplifies each process failure while replicas alone are not yet a safe standalone mitigation.
